title: A Phone Call About a Stolen Phone
script: Rafi: [warmly] Kak, someone took my phone at the market. I turned around for one second, and it was gone.
Sister: Okay, breathe first. Are you safe? That matters more than the phone right now.
Rafi: [curious] Yes, I'm safe, just shocked. I don't even know what to do first.
Sister: Good. First, use my phone to log into your account online, and lock the device remotely.
Rafi: [honestly] Can someone really open my apps and see my messages, my banking app, everything?
Sister: Not easily, if your screen has a passcode. That's why locking it now matters so much.
Rafi: [carefully] I never set up that remote-lock feature. I always meant to, but I kept putting it off.
Sister: Many people never do until something like this happens. Let's set it up on your new phone later.
Rafi: [thoughtful] What else should I do right now, before I go to the police?
Sister: Use official apps or websites to secure your email and financial accounts. Contact the mobile carrier to block the SIM too.
Rafi: [practically] I'm trying to remember what was saved on that phone. Photos, messages, my whole calendar.
Sister: Most of that is probably backed up somewhere, if your cloud backup was turned on.
Rafi: [reflective] I think it was, actually. I remember a message about backup completing last week.
Sister: Good. That's genuinely good news. Photos and contacts are usually the hardest things to lose.
Rafi: [encouraging] Okay. I’ll report it to the police, call the carrier and bank through official numbers, and watch for unusual account activity.
Sister: I'll come with you tomorrow. And next time, please turn on that remote-lock feature immediately.
Rafi: I promise. Today taught me that lesson the hard way.
Sister: [warmly] These things happen. What matters is you're safe, and we'll sort the rest out together.

quiz.question: What happened to Rafi at the market?
options: He forgot his phone at home
quiz.explanation: Rafi says someone took his phone at the market when he turned around for one second.

quiz.question: What does the sister ask Rafi to do first?
options: Use her phone to log in and lock the device remotely
quiz.explanation: The sister tells him to use her phone to log into his account and lock the device remotely.

quiz.question: What feature did Rafi never set up?
quiz.explanation: Rafi admits he never set up the remote-lock feature, though he always meant to.

quiz.question: What does the sister advise Rafi to change?
options: His important passwords, starting with email and banking
quiz.explanation: She advises him to change his important passwords, starting with his email and banking app.

quiz.question: Why is Rafi relieved about his photos and contacts?
options: His cloud backup was turned on
quiz.explanation: Rafi remembers a message about backup completing last week, so his data is likely saved.

quiz.question: What matters before the device?
quiz.explanation: His sister checks whether he is safe.

quiz.question: Where should account changes happen?
options: On a stranger’s phone without logout
quiz.explanation: Official access reduces another security risk.

quiz.question: Why contact the mobile carrier?
quiz.explanation: A stolen SIM may receive codes.

quiz.question: Who should be told about suspicious bank activity?
options: The bank through an official channel
